themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3900% spike with z-score of 14.74—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or enforcement breakdown in Throgs Neck/Co-op City this week.
evidence: 5 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
311 complaint data shows acute emergence, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview vendors and residents: are unlicensed food carts clustering in specific blocks?
Contact Department of Health: what triggered the sudden complaints this week—new vendor activity or enforcement operation?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance Crisis at Public Facilities
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 38 this week, up 881% from a baseline of 3.9 per week over 8 weeks (z-score: 10.48), indicating possible widespread facility breakdowns across parks, libraries, or NYCHA buildings in CD 210 this week.
evidence: 38 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget requests repeatedly ask for park building upgrades and library renovation, suggesting chronic facility issues
reporting_angles: Map the 38 complaints: are they concentrated at specific NYCHA buildings, parks, or libraries?
Investigate: did a heating system, water main, or electrical failure trigger cascading complaints across multiple facilities?

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 9 last week, up 620% from a baseline of 1.2 per week (z-score: 4.73), suggesting environmental stress, disease, or storm damage affecting the urban canopy in Throgs Neck/Co-op City over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Temporal clustering suggests acute event (storm, disease, or pest outbreak) rather than gradual decline
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department: what caused the spike—recent storm damage, pest infestation (emerald ash borer?), or disease?
Visual reporting: scout the neighborhood to identify the affected trees and assess canopy loss in specific blocks.

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Detection Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints increased to 5 last week, up 264% from a baseline of 1.4 per week (z-score: 4.23), potentially signaling elevated lead testing activity, water system contamination, or deteriorating paint in older housing stock in CD 210 over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 5 lead complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Throgs Neck/Co-op City has aging housing stock, including pre-1978 buildings vulnerable to lead paint
reporting_angles: Investigate: are complaints concentrated in NYCHA developments or private buildings? Contact HPD for lead violation data.
Interview families: are children being tested for lead exposure? Is the city supporting remediation?

themes_detail.label: Safety Concerns Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints jumped to 6 two weeks ago, up 700% from a baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score: 4.82), suggesting a localized safety incident, crime pattern, or hazardous condition that residents flagged in CD 210 over the past 2-3 weeks.
evidence: 6 safety complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
311 nature of complaints unclear; cross-reference with NYPD crime data and community reporting needed
reporting_angles: File FOIL for detailed 311 safety complaint descriptions: what specific hazards (structural, traffic, criminal activity) were flagged?
Interview residents and NYPD: was there a specific incident (accident, assault, structural collapse) two weeks ago?
